Package frc.spectrumLib.telemetry

Class SystemLoadMonitor

java.lang.Object
frc.spectrumLib.telemetry.SystemLoadMonitor
public class SystemLoadMonitor extends Object
Watches the things that made the robot fall behind on 2026-09-05 and says so on the dashboard.

That day the roboRIO CPU sat at 92 to 95 percent and the loop ran at 30 ms, and nothing on the Driver Station said so: the overrun watchdog is set to 200 ms and the CPU figure is buried in the DS log viewer. This publishes the numbers once a second and raises an Alert when one of them has been bad for long enough to matter:

  • CPU from /proc/stat, alert after 10.0 s at or above 85.0 percent.
  • Loop overruns: the share of loops longer than 25.0 ms, alert after 5.0 s above 50.0 percent.
  • Loop stall: a single loop over 200.0 ms while enabled, latched for 10.0 s so it is seen. Stalls while disabled are PathPlanner warmup and are ignored.
  • GC: collector time from the JVM, alert when one second carried 100.0 ms or more of it while enabled.
  • Memory: MemAvailable from /proc/meminfo, alert after 10.0 s under 24.0 MB.

Call periodic() once per loop, first thing in robotPeriodic(). Per loop it does a subtraction; once a second it reads two small files under /proc. Off the rio (no /proc) the CPU and memory channels go quiet and the rest keeps working.

    • periodic

      public void periodic()
      Records this loop and, once a second, samples the system and updates the alerts.

      Call once per loop, before anything else in robotPeriodic(), so the loop period it measures is the whole period.
